evidence.supportingExcerpt: The mitochondrial route uses BCL-2-family control of BAX and BAK and cytochrome c release. In cell experiments, combined BAX and BAK loss blocked mitochondrial responses to several apoptotic stimuli; this does not establish resistance to all forms of death. Death-receptor signals provide another route. Apoptosis is not inherently immune-silent: anthracycline-treated tumour cells showed calreticulin-dependent immunogenicity in mouse experiments. A death marker, a mitochondrial response and sustained killing answer different questions. Protein abundance alone cannot establish dependence or choose a treatment.

The BCL-2 family contains survival proteins, including BCL-2, BCL-XL and MCL-1; BH3-only stress mediators, including BIM, BID and PUMA; and pore-forming effectors BAX and BAK. In experimental cells, loss of both BAX and BAK blocked several mitochondrial apoptotic responses, rather than every possible form of death.

Cytochrome c moves from the mitochondrial intermembrane compartment, including crista stores, across the outer membrane to the cytosol. It does not begin in the matrix. The inner membrane separates these compartments; the spatial sketch is simplified, with no implied pore stoichiometry.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
The 2020 consensus defines immunogenic cell death through the adaptive immune response, not merely the appearance of dead cells. Antigens, appropriately timed danger signals, antigen-presenting cells and a responsive host all matter. Apoptotic or other death machinery does not by itself classify the immune outcome.

Calreticulin exposure, ATP or HMGB1 release and interferon-related signals are useful mechanistic readouts, but none alone proves protective immunity. Functional cross-priming and appropriate in-vivo immune tests address later steps. The consensus distinguishes mouse vaccination models from established disease; neither a surrogate marker nor a positive mouse assay establishes clinical benefit in a person.

In a local-treatment study, follow injury and signals through presentation, priming, recognition and measured tumour outcomes. Circulating cytokines or proliferating T cells alone do not establish tumour-specific killing, distant control or an optimal radiation dose.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immunogenic cell death is regulated death capable of initiating antigen-specific adaptive immunity in a compatible responding host. Antigenicity and appropriately timed adjuvant signals are both necessary considerations. It is an immune consequence, not an exclusive machine opposed to apoptosis or necrotic appearance.

In the consensus vaccination assay, remove residual inducing chemical and add no separate adjuvant before vaccinating immunocompetent syngeneic mice with dying tumour cells. Compare later challenge with living matched tumour cells in vaccinated and unvaccinated hosts, and test specificity with unrelated compatible tumour cells. Incidence and growth are functional readouts. Immune-competent versus deficient comparisons alone cannot isolate immunogenic death from other immunostimulation. Assays consume tumour-cell aliquots, supernatant or host-model material and report separate dead-cell fractions, signal concentrations or surface staining and challenge incidence or growth. Residual inducer, contamination, incompatible antigens and poor death confirmation can invalidate attribution. No universal DAMP cutoff establishes immunogenicity.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a phospholipid bilayer, heads face the watery surroundings on either side and tails face a shared inner core. An open ion channel provides a selective pore through that boundary. Net movement of a permitted ion follows its electrochemical gradient, which combines concentration and electrical effects; a drawing of inward flow does not set the direction for every ion or cell. This example is passive transport, rather than an ATP-driven pump or a route for a large cargo molecule. Uptake into a vesicle and escape across its membrane are separate events.

Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation and death. Cystine uptake through system xc- can support cysteine and glutathione availability; it does not transport glutathione itself. GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides, while FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q-associated defence. Dependence on these routes varies with the model and cellular conditions. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Macroautophagy encloses cargo in a double-membrane autophagosome, delivers it through lysosomal fusion and degrades it for reuse. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. Active recycling often supports stress adaptation, whereas autophagy-dependent death requires causal evidence implicating the machinery.

A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.

In a phospholipid bilayer, heads face the watery surroundings on either side and tails face a shared inner core. An open ion channel provides a selective pore through that boundary. Net movement of a permitted ion follows its electrochemical gradient, which combines concentration and electrical effects; a drawing of inward flow does not set the direction for every ion or cell. This example is passive transport, rather than an ATP-driven pump or a route for a large cargo molecule. Uptake into a vesicle and escape across its membrane are separate events.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. evidence.supportingExcerpt:

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
BRCA1 and BRCA2 name genes everyone normally carries. Interpret a reported variant by its classification, sample and origin, then assess the remaining allele and repair function. An uncertain BRCA2 variant with no normal sample and no remaining-copy assessment establishes neither inheritance nor biallelic loss nor current repair deficiency. Tumor purity and complex copy-number states can limit allele interpretation.

BRCA1 and BRCA2 have different repair roles. Brca1-deficient mouse embryonic stem cells had impaired homologous repair of defined chromosome breaks in Moynahan 1999. Purified full-length human BRCA2 promoted RAD51 assembly on single-stranded DNA in Jensen 2010. These model-specific results do not determine the effect of every human variant; the matching-template diagram omits many preparation and finishing steps.

In the CIMBA analysis, the invasive-breast-cancer results included 3,797 BRCA1 and 2,392 BRCA2 carriers, with individual marker data available for varying subsets. Among tumors with relevant marker information, 68% in BRCA1 carriers and 16% in BRCA2 carriers were triple-negative. These are pathology proportions among cancers in mutation carriers, not the chance that an individual carrier develops cancer or that a person with triple-negative disease carries a BRCA variant. Age and ascertainment matter.

Repair capacity can change after treatment. In the selected eight-person resistant metastatic breast cancer cohort of Waks 2020, four acquired definite or putative BRCA reversions; other mechanisms could restore repair too. A reversion can restore a disrupted reading frame, while old genomic patterns remain. This selected cohort does not establish a common or most-frequent mechanism across all breast cancers, and a single tissue or blood sample can miss heterogeneous reversions.

A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A mutational signature is a distribution over mutation categories inferred from a catalog of calls. It does not attach an observed cause to every mutation. Several processes can overlap, some causes remain unknown, and a classifier of BRCA-related repair deficiency is not a model of a patient's probability of drug response. Its endpoint and validation population must be named.

Single-base substitutions change one base, doublet substitutions change adjacent bases, and indels insert or delete sequence. In a fictional four-category exercise, template A has percentages 40, 30, 20, 10 and B has 30, 40, 20, 10. For 100 mutations, a 50/50 mixture gives 35, 35, 20, 10; a 60/40 mixture gives 36, 34, 20, 10. The close reconstructions illustrate ambiguity; these are arithmetic examples, not fitted SBS3 data or observed biological results.

HRDetect combines six weighted features, including microhomology-associated deletions, substitution signatures 3 and 8, rearrangement signatures 3 and 5 and a scar index. It is not simply an SBS3-positive call. In the original study, applying genome-trained weights to exome-like data reduced sensitivity to 46.8%; retraining improved it to 73% while adding calls not made by the genome model. Missing rearrangements and sparse substitutions are consequential, so panel, exome and whole-genome implementations require separate validation, uncertainty and fit checks.

Roberts analyzed 954,247 mutations across 2,680 exomes from 14 cancer types; the APOBEC pattern reached 68% of mutations in some samples, not in every breast cancer. HRDetect reported 98.7% sensitivity and 124 high-scoring tumors among 560 breast cancers, about 22%, under its study definition. That selected cohort estimate is not a population prevalence or a clinical response probability. DNA quality, variant-calling errors, signature competition, catalog and software versions remain part of interpretation.

proofs.requirement: Parental DNA opens ahead of a moving fork and newly synthesized strands trail behind, including a simplified discontinuous strand.
proofs.sourceReadBasis: Full source-body reads recorded in completed-read-receipts.json; native/source/canonical acceptance remains separate.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: At a moving replication fork, the unopened parental duplex lies ahead of the junction. New complementary DNA accumulates behind it on the parental templates. One new strand is made continuously toward the advancing fork; the lagging strand is made in short pieces that are later joined. Both are synthesised in the 5-prime to 3-prime direction. A shorter labelled track at the same pulse duration describes less DNA copied along the measured molecule, rather than a shorter labelling interval or proof of chromosome breakage.

In G1, ORC binds origins and with CDC6 and CDT1 loads double MCM2-7 hexamers (licensing). At S-phase entry CDK2 and DDK (CDC7) convert MCM into the active CMG helicase (with CDC45, GINS), recruiting polymerases: Pol α-primase starts, Pol ε (leading) and Pol δ (lagging) extend, with PCNA as clamp, RPA coating single strands, and Okazaki fragments joined by FEN1/LIG1. Re-licensing within one cycle is prevented by CDT1 degradation (CRL4-CDT2), geminin, and CDK activity. Oncogenes (MYC, cyclin E, RAS) shorten G1, fire excess and ectopic origins, and cause origin-fork collisions and dNTP exhaustion, the root of replication stress. Chemotherapy exploits this: antimetabolites deplete dNTPs (5-FU, methotrexate, pemetrexed, hydroxyurea inhibits RNR) or terminate chains (gemcitabine, cytarabine); topoisomerase I poisons (irinotecan, topotecan, ADC payloads SN-38, DXd, exatecan) trap the enzyme ahead of the fork; platinum crosslinks block polymerases. POLQ, POLA1 and CDC7 inhibitors are experimental.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Replication stress concerns difficulty copying DNA, including slow or stalled forks. A stalled fork can be protected and restart; it is not automatically a broken chromosome. Checkpoint activation, recovery, incomplete copying, damage and death are separate stages and measurements. High checkpoint-gene RNA or rapid proliferation alone does not establish fork stress, dependence or drug sensitivity.

RPA coats exposed single-stranded DNA and helps recruit ATR through ATRIP, initiating checkpoint signaling in biochemical and cellular experiments. Activated H-Ras in normal human-cell models produced hyper-replication before damage signaling and senescence. Bester studied HPV E6/E7 or cyclin-E-driven models in which nucleotide limitation disturbed replication and nucleoside supplementation in culture improved dynamics. These experiments do not recommend supplements or predict the behavior of every oncogene-bearing tumor.

In a fictional DNA-combing exercise, live cells receive a 30-minute IdU pulse followed by a 30-minute CldU pulse. At the stated example stretching calibration of 2 kilobases per micrometre, a 7.5-micrometre second track represents 15 kilobases copied in 30 minutes, or 0.5 kilobases per minute; a 15-micrometre track gives 1 kilobase per minute. Bester used those pulse times and calibration, but these example lengths are not that study's results and the calibration is not universal.

DNA-fiber measurements require viable cells that incorporate labels; extraction destroys sampled cells. Ordinary fixed pathology cannot retrospectively supply live-label tracks. Document pulse timing, labeling, stretching, track selection, cell-cycle distribution, model and comparison group. A lower population S-phase fraction is distinct from the speed of one selected molecule. Track length alone establishes neither the cause, breaks, restart nor death; checkpoint dependence needs a targeted perturbation and a separate functional outcome, without a universal patient-positive cutoff.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The unfolded protein response has distinct outputs. IRE1-dependent processing of XBP1 RNA produces a potent transcriptional regulator; total XBP1 message and its spliced fraction are different measurements. PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and can reduce translation initiation. ER stress also promotes ATF6 proteolysis, releasing a fragment that acts in the nucleus. These findings come from molecular and cell experiments. Branch activity, adaptation, survival dependence and treatment benefit require separate evidence. Specify branch, timing, total protein or RNA controls and direct growth and death measurements.

ER stress is an imbalance between protein-folding demand and local capacity; the unfolded protein response is an adaptation programme, not the same thing as the stress. IRE1 processes XBP1 RNA, PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and ATF6 processing releases a nuclear regulator. Distinct branches can alter folding capacity, incoming translation and disposal.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A mitochondrion has an outer membrane and a folded inner membrane. The space between them is the intermembrane space; the matrix is enclosed by the inner membrane. Each membrane is a phospholipid bilayer, with two leaflets rather than being a single leaflet of a shared membrane. Electron transfer ends with oxygen reduced to water, while some complexes pump protons across the inner membrane. These distinct processes do not give a universal conversion from oxygen use to ATP production.

In a phospholipid bilayer, heads face the watery surroundings on either side and tails face a shared inner core. An open ion channel provides a selective pore through that boundary. Net movement of a permitted ion follows its electrochemical gradient, which combines concentration and electrical effects; a drawing of inward flow does not set the direction for every ion or cell. This example is passive transport, rather than an ATP-driven pump or a route for a large cargo molecule. Uptake into a vesicle and escape across its membrane are separate events.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In mitochondria, respiratory electron transfer and proton movement are distinct processes. Some respiratory complexes move protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space; return through ATP synthase can support ATP formation, while other return pathways dissipate the gradient without that synthesis step. These directions do not specify a fixed proton-to-ATP ratio. Protons return from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the membrane-embedded Fo part of ATP synthase. The matrix-facing F1 part uses the transferred energy to make ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. Protons provide the driving force; they are not converted into ATP. A parallel proton leak bypasses ATP synthase and dissipates the gradient. In Racker and Stoeckenius' reconstituted vesicles, a light-driven membrane system from Halobacterium supported ATP formation when mitochondrial ATPase was included. Their artificial vesicles pumped in the opposite direction to the intact source cells, so the experiment supports coupling without specifying a universal cellular orientation or ratio.

A mitochondrion has an outer membrane and a folded inner membrane. The space between them is the intermembrane space; the matrix is enclosed by the inner membrane. Each membrane is a phospholipid bilayer, with two leaflets rather than being a single leaflet of a shared membrane. Electron transfer ends with oxygen reduced to water, while some complexes pump protons across the inner membrane. These distinct processes do not give a universal conversion from oxygen use to ATP production.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.

In mitochondria, respiratory electron transfer and proton movement are distinct processes. Some respiratory complexes move protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space; return through ATP synthase can support ATP formation, while other return pathways dissipate the gradient without that synthesis step. These directions do not specify a fixed proton-to-ATP ratio. Protons return from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the membrane-embedded Fo part of ATP synthase. The matrix-facing F1 part uses the transferred energy to make ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. Protons provide the driving force; they are not converted into ATP. A parallel proton leak bypasses ATP synthase and dissipates the gradient. In Racker and Stoeckenius' reconstituted vesicles, a light-driven membrane system from Halobacterium supported ATP formation when mitochondrial ATPase was included. Their artificial vesicles pumped in the opposite direction to the intact source cells, so the experiment supports coupling without specifying a universal cellular orientation or ratio.

In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
BRD4 is a chromatin reader that recognizes acetylated histones and helps regulate transcription. Its recognition pockets and other protein interactions can contribute different functions.

Engaging an acetyl-recognition pocket and depleting a whole protein are different interventions. In selected TNBC models with acquired BET-inhibitor resistance, cells remained dependent on BRD4 through bromodomain-independent regulation. Verify pocket engagement and depletion independently before comparing growth outcomes. Neither operation alone establishes clinical benefit or a vulnerability caused by an uncharacterized BET-family variant.

BET proteins read acetylated lysine marks; they do not write the acetyl mark. The family includes BRD2, BRD3, BRD4 and BRDT, with two bromodomains and an extra-terminal interaction region. BRD4 can recruit transcription-elongation machinery, but other bromodomain proteins are not all BET proteins and family members are not functionally interchangeable. A schematic that retains the same histone mark during pocket occupation and protein depletion isolates two different interventions. The fixed mark is a drawing convention rather than a measured unchanged acetylation state; the state of the mark needs its own measurement. A representative pocket also does not make JQ1 specific to BD1.

In a fictional culture, an engaged BET pocket probe leaves growth unchanged while independently controlled BRD4 depletion impairs growth. The findings can coexist if the remaining protein supplies functions the probe does not block, as the resistant-model work illustrates. Binding assays, chromatin occupancy, early RNA changes, later growth and death, general transcription effects and appropriate restoration controls answer different questions. Lower MYC RNA alone does not attribute a later effect to MYC.

French identified a BRD4-NUT fusion in the defined carcinoma; a fusion is a different biological alteration from an ordinary sequence variant. Stathis reported four people with confirmed BRD4-NUT carcinomas treated with OTX015/MK-8628 in compassionate use: two had rapid regression, with no randomized comparison or established survival benefit. The report described thrombocytopenia, including reversible grade 3 events and a grade 4 event in one patient. This small selected series does not establish efficacy across BET-altered tumors.

A schematic that retains the same histone mark during pocket occupation and protein depletion isolates two different interventions. The fixed mark is a drawing convention rather than a measured unchanged acetylation state; the state of the mark needs its own measurement. A representative pocket also does not make JQ1 specific to BD1.

In a fictional culture, an engaged BET pocket probe leaves growth unchanged while independently controlled BRD4 depletion impairs growth. Binding assays, chromatin occupancy, early RNA changes, later growth and death, general transcription effects and appropriate restoration controls answer different questions. Lower MYC RNA alone does not attribute a later effect to MYC.

French identified a BRD4-NUT fusion in the defined carcinoma; a fusion is a different biological alteration from an ordinary sequence variant. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
NFE2L2 encodes NRF2, a transcription factor; KEAP1 is an adaptor linking it to a CUL3-containing ubiquitin-ligase complex. Under suitable unstressed conditions, tagging promotes NRF2 degradation. Reduced turnover can make more NRF2 available for nuclear stress-defense programs. Protein turnover, nuclear output, protection against a stressor and survival dependence require separate measurements.

Zhang's biochemical and cell experiments found stress-associated inhibition of NRF2 ubiquitination without disruption of every KEAP1-NRF2 association. The lesson's paired conditions depict altered turnover, not creation of NRF2 or a mandatory physical latch release. CUL3 is a scaffold used with other adaptors and substrates, so a CUL3 change cannot be assigned an NRF2 effect from its name alone.

In a fictional culture, high NQO1 RNA, nuclear NRF2, several responsive proteins and reduced readouts after controlled KEAP1 restoration support a regulatory consequence. Test survival under a defined stress separately, using a specific NRF2 perturbation, matched controls and appropriate restoration to assess dependence. Stronger defenses may confer resistance; their abundance does not demonstrate ferroptosis sensitivity or benefit from an NRF2-directed therapy.

Singh sequenced 54 non-small-cell lung tumors and found KEAP1 mutations in ten, about 19%, alongside a separate 12-cell-line analysis. This cohort proportion is not a universal lung-cancer prevalence. Vartanian's proteomic study in A549 and other cell experiments found that brusatol broadly inhibited protein synthesis, so lower NRF2 after that compound does not establish selective engagement. Use cell identity, preservation, timing, several outputs and general-translation controls; no universal NRF2-high treatment cutoff follows.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
The full-length androgen receptor is a hormone-binding protein that can regulate transcription. Its interactions with other proteins, receptor form and cellular setting affect its activity.

Receptor amount, location, transcription and growth dependence are different observations. Nuclear AR immunostaining reports protein in sampled cells; a luminal androgen receptor, or LAR, label is a versioned RNA-classifier result. TBCRC 032 correlative analyses found AR protein expression alone insufficient to identify AR-dependent tumors. Neither staining nor classifier membership alone proves patient benefit.

Full-length AR has distinct regions for transcriptional regulation, DNA binding and ligand binding. Androgens can change receptor interactions, nuclear localization and regulatory-DNA binding, with effects determined by partners, accessible DNA and receptor form. Tran's antiandrogen experiments in prostate models tested binding, nuclear movement and transcriptional effects separately. An RNA signal does not characterize a truncated protein or transfer those prostate results to breast-cancer treatment.

A fictional tumor with 20% AR-positive nuclei but a non-LAR RNA classification need not have a mistaken result. The assays measure different layers; compare antibody, scoring, tumor-cell content, preservation, sampling, normalization and classifier version. Twenty percent stained nuclei is not twenty percent of patients expected to respond. Dependence requires a controlled receptor perturbation with downstream and growth or survival measurements.

Lehmann 2016 refined TNBCtype from six classes to four tumor-specific classes after immune and stromal contributions explained the former immunomodulatory and mesenchymal stem-like signals. LAR does not mean estrogen-receptor-positive disease. TBCRC 032 was a defined phase Ib/II metastatic breast-cancer study of enzalutamide with or without taselisib, with phase II focused on AR-positive TNBC; its exploratory correlations do not turn an RNA subtype into a universal treatment rule or import a prostate indication.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.

Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.

Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study treated 94 people with advanced solid tumours. AXIN2 RNA decreased in 94 per cent of 52 paired skin-biopsy comparisons and 74 per cent of 35 paired tumour-biopsy comparisons; no RECIST responses were observed. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Extracellular matrix includes fibrous proteins such as collagen and fibronectin and carbohydrate-rich molecules such as proteoglycans. Cells produce it; the matrix is not itself a living-cell population. Basement membrane is a specialised matrix, while connective tissue and stroma include cells as well. Production, enzymatic breakdown and crosslinking can change its amount and organisation over time.

Amount, fibre orientation, pore architecture, density, stiffness and cell behaviour are different features. Stiffness describes resistance to deformation, often expressed as a modulus in pascals; the result depends on the measurement scale, preparation and loading. Collagen-stained area and collagen RNA do not directly measure stiffness. Salmon’s viable human lung-tumour slices linked architecture and T-cell movement under the studied conditions; the result does not establish the mechanism in every breast tumour.

In a fictional pair of equal-area fields with eight equal-size fibres each, equal drawn collagen area can accompany different architecture. Independently stipulated mean T-cell speeds of 4 micrometres per minute do not establish equal directions, entry into tumour nests, contact with cancer cells or stiffness. Cell positions outside nests alone do not show that matrix caused them; other signals may contribute. Separate the structural observation, live movement measurement and causal perturbation, then assess any clinical claim with its own evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Clonal evolution concerns inherited lineage features and changing population composition through variation, selection and chance. Drivers can contribute to behaviour while passengers accompany them. A newly detected variant may already have existed below the earlier detection limit. Selection and fitness depend on location, nutrients, immunity and treatment, rather than simply the fastest growth or a universal measure of danger.

Nowell proposed an evolutionary framework; Gerlinger’s multiregion study of four renal cancers supplied evidence for branching in its sampled setting. Neither study is a census of every tumour. Genetic drift is chance-driven change in variant frequency, and bottlenecks can change composition without the same selective explanation. A frequency change alone does not identify drift, selection or resistance. Williams tested a defined neutral-growth model in which newly arising variants have no further fitness differences during the modelled expansion, relating frequencies to mutation timing. Tarabichi showed why a good frequency-model fit is not sufficient proof of neutrality or the absence of historical selection.

Sequencing read fractions and inferred cancer-cell fractions are different quantities, affected by purity, copy number and detection limits. Compare appropriate regional or time samples for shared and differing alterations, or trace labelled descendants experimentally, retaining date, location, resolution and uncertainty. An expression cluster is not automatically a genetic clone. A dominant sampled branch does not count every lesion or establish target coverage in unseen disease.

proofs.requirement: The selected base-excision job removes an altered base, with the resulting gap rebuilt rather than the response signal proving completion.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Removing a lesion starts a repair job; synthesis and sealing complete it. In a selected base-excision route, a damaged base is removed, the backbone is processed and the gap is rebuilt and sealed. Nucleotide-excision repair cuts out a lesion-containing stretch, then fills and seals the patch. Mismatch repair replaces the incorrectly copied strand segment using the other strand as a template. These are different repair jobs; detecting a checkpoint signal does not demonstrate that any was completed.

Damaged bases (8-oxoguanine, uracil, alkylated bases from temozolomide or endogenous methylation) are removed by glycosylases (OGG1, UNG, MPG), APE1 cuts the backbone, PARP1 binds the single-strand break and PARylates itself and histones to recruit XRCC1, Pol β fills the gap and LIG3 seals it (short-patch) or FEN1/LIG1 (long-patch). PARP inhibitors compete with NAD+ and, crucially, trap PARP1 on DNA (talazoparib >> olaparib > veliparib in trapping potency), so replication forks collide with the complex and collapse into double-strand breaks that only HR can fix, the mechanistic basis of BRCA synthetic lethality; PARP1-selective saruparib spares PARP2 and bone marrow. O6-methylguanine, the lethal TMZ lesion, is reversed directly by MGMT; MGMT promoter methylation predicts TMZ benefit in glioblastoma, and MMR is needed for TMZ toxicity. PARP inhibition also traps PARP at oxidative lesions from radiation and generates cytosolic DNA that fires cGAS-STING.

proofs.subject: dna-damage
proofs.requirement: The selected mismatch-repair job corrects the copied strand error rather than treating either mismatched letter as a new established mutation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.

Removing a lesion starts a repair job; synthesis and sealing complete it. In a selected base-excision route, a damaged base is removed, the backbone is processed and the gap is rebuilt and sealed. Nucleotide-excision repair cuts out a lesion-containing stretch, then fills and seals the patch. Mismatch repair replaces the incorrectly copied strand segment using the other strand as a template. These are different repair jobs; detecting a checkpoint signal does not demonstrate that any was completed.

MutSα (MSH2-MSH6) recognises base mismatches and small insertion-deletion loops, MutSβ (MSH2-MSH3) larger loops; MutLα (MLH1-PMS2) is recruited and nicks the new strand, EXO1 excises, Pol δ resynthesises, LIG1 seals. Loss of MLH1 (usually by promoter hypermethylation in sporadic colorectal and endometrial cancer, often with BRAF V600E), MSH2, MSH6 or PMS2 (germline in Lynch syndrome, or EPCAM deletion silencing MSH2) produces microsatellite instability (MSI-H), a hypermutator phenotype with 10-100x more mutations, frameshift neoantigens, and the SBS6/15/26 signatures. Clinically MSI-H/dMMR is tumour-agnostic for pembrolizumab and dostarlimab; dMMR rectal cancer can be cured with dostarlimab alone (complete responses in >90% of patients in the MSK study); neoadjuvant nivolumab-ipilimumab gives near-universal pathological responses in dMMR colon cancer. MMR loss also confers tolerance to temozolomide and thiopurines (the lesions are no longer recognised). Synthetic lethality: MSI-H cells depend on the WRN helicase; WRN inhibitors are in trials.

semanticAssessment.explanation: The copied strand is replaced using the other as template; a mismatch is distinguished from an established mutation. Retained clinical assertions in the companion pathway are outside this certification.
